extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners/attorneys, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements, timing, and documentation for claiming foreign priority (including restoration petitions, certified priority copies, translations, inventor's certificates, and PCT/national-stage rules) in U.S. patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of right of priority under 37 CFR 1.55(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restoration of the right of priority is available for priority claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)–(d) or (f), 365(a) or (b), or 386(a) or (b); it permits claiming priority to a foreign application filed up to fourteen months earlier (or eight months for a design application). A petition to restore the right of priority filed on or after May 13, 2015, must be filed in the subsequent application, or in the earliest nonprovisional application claiming benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c) to the subsequent application, if such subsequent application is not a nonprovisional application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the subsequent application is not a nonprovisional, file the petition in the earliest nonprovisional claiming benefit. If restoration is granted, no further petition under 37 CFR 1.55(c) is required in applications entitled to claim the benefit; file a copy of the decision granting restoration with any application claiming the subsequent application and the foreign application so the Office recognizes restoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific petition contents for 37 CFR 1.55(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.55(c) requires: (A) the priority claim in an application data sheet identifying the foreign application by application number, country (or intellectual property authority), day, month, and year of its filing (unless previously submitted); (B) the petition fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m); and (C) a statement that the delay in filing the subsequent application within the twelve-month period (or six-month period for a design application) was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of restoration vis-à-vis pre-AIA statutory bars
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if restoration under 37 CFR 1.55(c) allows a priority claim to a foreign application filed up to fourteen months earlier (or eight months for a design application), an application examined under pre-AIA first-to-invent laws may still be subject to the 12-month statutory time periods in pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) and (d) measured from the U.S. filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration of priority does not necessarily protect against rejections under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) or (d); see MPEP §§ 2133 and 2135 et seq.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to file claim for priority and certified copy within pendency (37 CFR 1.55(g)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim for priority and the certified copy of the foreign application (as specified in 35 U.S.C. 119(b) or PCT Rule 17) must be filed within the pendency of the application, unless filed with a petition under paragraph (e) or (f) of this section, or with a petition accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.17(g) showing good and sufficient cause for delay in a design application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the claim or certified copy is filed after payment of the issue fee, the patent will not include the priority claim unless corrected by a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and 37 CFR 1.323. The pendency requirement does not supersede other timing rules in 37 CFR 1.55.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances where Office may require earlier filing or translation (37 CFR 1.55(g)(2)–(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require that the claim for priority and the certified copy be filed earlier than otherwise provided when: (i) the application is involved in an interference or derivation proceeding; (ii) when necessary to overcome the date of a reference relied upon by the examiner; or (iii) when deemed necessary by the examiner. An English language translation of a non-English foreign application is not required except in those same circumstances or when specifically required by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translation is required, it must be a translation of the certified copy and must be filed together with a statement that the translation of the certified copy is accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy filing consequences and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: The certified copy must be filed in all cases even if not necessary during pendency to overcome a reference. Applicants are encouraged to check Patent Center to verify the International Bureau has forwarded the certified copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a certified copy of the priority document was submitted in compliance with PCT Rule 17 during the international phase, the copy received from the International Bureau is acceptable. If the International Bureau is unable to forward a copy because applicant failed to submit it, the applicant must provide a certified copy or have the Office retrieve it via the priority document exchange during national stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventor's certificates as basis for priority (37 CFR 1.55(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: An inventor's certificate may form the basis for rights of priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(d) only when the country filing it gives applicants, at their discretion, the right to apply either for a patent or for an inventor's certificate for the same subject matter. To claim priority on that basis, the applicant must include an affidavit or declaration stating that, upon investigation, the affiant is satisfied that the applicant had the option to file for either a patent or an inventor's certificate when filing the inventor's certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The affidavit/declaration requirement is only to show that the option generally existed in that country for the subject matter; it is not intended to probe eligibility of the particular applicant. Priority rights will be honored only if the applicant had the option/discretion in the home country; certain countries issue inventor's certificates only for certain subject matter, which affects applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing priority claim in original 35 U.S.C. 111(a) applications (37 CFR 1.55(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: For original applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), the claim for priority must be filed within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application, except as provided in paragraph (e). These time periods do not apply to design applications or applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) before November 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on or after September 16, 2012, the priority claim must be presented in an application data sheet (§ 1.76(b)(6)). If not presented within the time periods, the claim is considered waived but may be accepted if accompanied by a grantable petition showing the delay was unintentional (see MPEP § 214.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing priority claim and certified copy in national stage (35 U.S.C. 371 / PCT Rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an international application entering the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, the claim for priority and a certified copy of the foreign application must be filed within the time limits set forth in the PCT and the PCT Regulations, except as provided in 37 CFR 1.55(e). For certified copies where national stage commenced on or after December 18, 2013, a certified copy not filed during the international stage must be filed within the later of four months from national stage commencement, four months from initial submission under 35 U.S.C. 371, or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application (subject to exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is permissible, but not required, to present the claim for priority in an application data sheet in an international application entering the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Rule 4.10 — required contents of a priority claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Any priority claim must be made in the Request and consist of a statement claiming priority of an earlier application and must indicate: (i) the filing date of the earlier application; (ii) the number of the earlier application; (iii) for national applications, the country in which it was filed; (iv) for regional applications, the authority entrusted with granting regional patents; and (v) for international applications, the receiving Office with which it was filed. Additional indications are required for regional/international earlier applications (e.g., countries for which that earlier application was filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the purposes of these paragraphs, Article 2(vi) shall not apply. A priority claim may be corrected or added in accordance with PCT Rule 26 bis.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Rule 17 — priority document submission and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Where priority of an earlier national or international application is claimed, a copy of that earlier application certified by the authority with which it was filed (the priority document) shall be submitted to the International Bureau or the receiving Office not later than 16 months after the priority date, subject to specified exceptions (Rule 17.1). The receiving Office may prepare and transmit the priority document to the International Bureau upon request (subject to a fee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If none of the Rule 17.1(a)/(b)/(b‑bis) requirements is complied with, any designated Office may, subject to reasonable opportunity to furnish the document, disregard the priority claim. The International Bureau will furnish copies to designated Offices upon request after international publication (subject to conditions). Priority documents may be obtained from digital libraries per Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO practice for international applications (37 CFR 1.451)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim for priority must, subject to paragraph (d), be made on the Request (PCT Rule 4.10) in a manner complying with Administrative Instructions sections 110 and 115. When the priority of an earlier U.S. national application or international application filed with the U.S. Receiving Office is claimed, the applicant may request that the USPTO prepare a certified copy of the prior application for transmittal to the International Bureau; the fee is set forth in § 1.19(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a certified copy is not submitted together with the international application, or the request/fee for preparation is not filed within 16 months of the priority date, the certified copy must be furnished by the applicant to the International Bureau or the U.S. Receiving Office within the time limit specified in PCT Rule 17.1(a). Applicants may correct or add a priority claim under PCT Rule 26 bis.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of late or unintentionally delayed priority claims (37 CFR 1.55(d) & (e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims for foreign priority not presented within the time period specified in 37 CFR 1.55 are considered waived. A claim presented after the time period may be accepted if it includes the required identification information and is accompanied by a grantable petition to accept the unintentionally delayed claim for priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 214.02 for procedural treatment of unintentionally delayed priority claims and the specific petition content and fee requirements.
